title: Compatible weakly contractible hypercovers from a common profinite component space
statement:
Let $h:X'\to X$ be a morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] with w-strictly local coordinate rings [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Suppose $\pi_0(h)$ is a homeomorphism and identify both profinite component spaces with $P=\pi_0(X)$, with the quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. Work in compatible small-site universes [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a profinite $P$-space $S$, write $X\times_P S$ and $X'\times_P S$ for the relative component lifts, defined by inverse limits of finite clopen subdivisions [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site]. Then there exists an augmented simplicial profinite space $S_\bullet\to P$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] such that every $S_n$ is extremally disconnected (closures of opens are open), every $S_n\to P$ is surjective, and every matching arrow is surjective. Here the degree-zero matching space is $P$ and higher matching spaces are the finite limits of compatible proper faces over $P$.
The levelwise lifts $U_n=X\times_P S_n$ and $V_n=X'\times_P S_n$ form augmented simplicial objects $U_\bullet\to X$ and $V_\bullet\to X'$ of their full small pro-etale sites. Every matching arrow of each is a pro-etale covering. Their terms are affine with w-contractible coordinate rings and are weakly contractible site objects, meaning that evaluation of set sheaves there sends epimorphisms to surjections [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. The canonical component maps identify $\pi_0(U_n)$ and $\pi_0(V_n)$ with $S_n$. There are canonical maps $g_n:V_n\to U_n$ over $h$ inducing $\operatorname{id}_{S_n}$ and commuting with every face, degeneracy and augmentation.
In addition, for either $T=\operatorname{Spec}C$ in $\{X,X'\}$ and each $n$, the lift $T\times_P S_n$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}D_n$ over $T$ and $S_n$, where
$$C_Z=\varinjlim_{W\supset Z}C_{e_W},\qquad D_n=\varinjlim_{\mathcal Q}\prod_{A\in\mathcal Q}C_{t_n(A)}.$$
Here $t_n:S_n\to P$ is the augmentation, $Z$ is a closed subset of $P$, $W$ runs over its clopen neighbourhoods ordered by reverse inclusion, $e_W$ is the idempotent whose localization cuts out the clopen inverse image of $W$ in $T$, and $\mathcal Q$ runs over finite partitions into nonempty clopen subsets, with the natural refinement maps. The topology of this lift is $|T|\times_P S_n$, its local ring at $(x,s)$ is $\mathcal O_{T,x}$, and its closed-point space is $S_n$. The empty case is allowed, with the empty scheme and the empty product ring.

proof.text: Apply the Stonean hypercover existence theorem to P = affineComponentSpace X. It supplies the common simplicial object S, its matching cones, extremal disconnectedness, and every augmentation surjectivity.

Apply the single-base lifting theorem to X with the identity component homeomorphism and to X′ with e inverse, using the same S and its hypercover properties. This supplies U,p and V,q with all matching, affine, weak-contractibility, topology, stalk, component, closed-point and normalized ring-model clauses.

For each n, the homeomorphism for V identifies the component label of its structural image in X′ with e inverse(t_n(q_n(x))). The hypothesis on h and e therefore makes (h(v_n(x)),q_n(x)) a point of the pullback describing U_n. Compose this continuous pair with the inverse homeomorphism for U_n. Lift the resulting continuous map uniquely to a scheme map g_n over X by stalk-isomorphism lifting. Its two coordinates give v_n followed by h and q_n, proving both augmentation and profinite-coordinate compatibility.

Any two scheme maps into U_n with equal composites to X and equal p_n coordinates have equal underlying continuous maps: the two components of their images under its pullback homeomorphism are equal. Uniqueness in stalk-isomorphism lifting then makes the scheme maps equal. For each simplicial operator, the composites V_m to U_n have equal maps to X by the slice equations, and equal profinite coordinates by the naturality of p and q and the identity p_n g_n = q_n. Apply that uniqueness to obtain all required operator equations. This also works for empty spaces, with no chosen points or nonemptiness assumptions.

Steps 8–9 hold: g_n comes from the unique stalkwise lift, the operator equations follow by uniqueness, and the empty case is handled by the empty partition. I tested h = id, P = point and P = ∅.
